title: Veil of ignorance
summary: Design society's rules before knowing which role in it you'll get.
intro: Before any of these rules exist, imagine you'll be assigned a random role in the society they create — rich or poor, healthy or sick, talented or not. You don't know which yet. Design the rules first.

questions.prompt: How much should society guarantee the worst-off, even if it costs the best-off more?
questions.minLabel: Let outcomes stand as they fall

questions.prompt: Two societies. A: everyone gets a modest, guaranteed income. B: most people do very well, but 1 in 20 ends up in severe poverty with no safety net. Not knowing which role you'd get, which do you join?

options.label: Society B — higher average, real chance of poverty

questions.prompt: You can require insurance against ending up disabled and unable to work. It costs 5% of everyone's income, including the healthy majority who will never need it.

options.label: No mandatory insurance — let people keep the 5%

questions.prompt: Some people are born with talents that earn far more, through no effort of their own. Should the rules tax that luck to help those born less fortunate?

options.label: Tax it some, but let talent still pay off
No — what you're born with is yours to keep

questions.prompt: The rules are set. Now your role is assigned at random — you could be anyone in this society, including its worst-off member. Do you still endorse the rules you chose?
questions.scenario: This is the actual test of a rule made behind the veil: would you accept it as the person who drew the worst position?

options.label: Yes — I'd still accept these rules
No — I'd want to change them
